newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-PIPPEN STAYS BULLS' ONLY FINALS TRIPLE-DOUBLE MAN.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-PIPPEN STAYS BULLS' ONLY FINALS TRIPLE-DOUBLE MAN.

text.p: Scottie Pippen missed an easy layup towards the end of the Bulls' decisive victory over the Utah Jazz Wednesday, costing Michael Jordan his first Finals triple-double.

Jordan, playing in his fifth NBA Finals series, finished with 38 points, 13 rebounds and nine assists, and Pippen had some fun when a reporter gently broached the subject by saying: "Michael was one assist shy of a triple-double."
"Yes and no. I had an opportunity, I should have made the layup, and it didn't fall. I guess it wasn't meant to be."
Pippen didn't know he was the only Bull ever to achieve a triple-double in the NBA Finals, but when so informed, quipped: "So I didn't want him to tie me, then."
Pippen had a good excuse. He reinjured his left foot on the first play of the game trying to block a shot by Bryon Russell.

"I went to block his shot from behind," said Pippen. "I just had a bad landing. It pretty much took me out of my game, had me frustrated. I wanted to be much more aggressive ... but after I aggravated it, it was pretty painful throughout the game."

Asked if he had given Pippen a hard time for missing the shot, Jordan said: "He apologised before I said anything. And I'd rather have a healthy Scottie Pippen than a triple-double, no matter how you look at it.
"He's playing with a courageous attitude just by being out there."
But Jordan could not resist ending his news conference with one last shot at Pippen.
"He suits up every day and as long as he's dressing I'm pretty sure he feels he can play. I just hope he can make a layup or two next game," Jordan said, snickering.
"He didn't need that triple-double," said Pippen. "He's got everything."
